\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMExample}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Language of valid plain strings]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.validPlainLang}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.validPlainLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ValidPlain}
The valid plain language is the set of Boolean strings that satisfy the validity
condition for plain strings.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Valid-input guessing program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NARM}
A one-register nondeterministic register program with no oracle deciders and four
instruction labels is defined as follows: at label $0$ it chooses label $1$ or $2$; at
label $1$ it checks whether the input is a valid plain encoding, continuing to label $3$
if so and rejecting otherwise; labels $2$ and $3$ halt with answers false and true,
respectively.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Halting of the valid-input checker]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA_halts}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA_halts}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.choose, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.det, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.halted, Complexity.LogProg.ValidPlain, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA}
\difficulty{5}
For every Boolean input word $x$, every predicate $G$ on configurations of the checker,
and every oracle with no query indices, suppose $G$ holds for each configuration whose
program state is any of the four states and whose sole register is zero, regardless of
its answer component. Then every sequence of three choice bits, starting from the
prescribed initial configuration, halts after those three steps; at every earlier time
when the computation has not yet halted, its configuration satisfies $G$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Acceptance of the valid-input checker]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA_ans}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA_ans}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.NAns, Complexity.LogProg.ValidPlain, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA, Complexity.LogProg.nans_choose, Complexity.LogProg.nans_det, Complexity.LogProg.nans_halted}
\difficulty{5}
For every Boolean input word $x$ and every oracle with no query indices, the
nondeterministic program that guesses a branch and checks whether its input is valid
accepts in exactly three steps from its prescribed initial configuration if and only if
$x$ has the form $\langle 1^n,w\rangle$ for some $n$ and some canonical binary word $w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Logarithmic-space recognition of valid encodings]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.validPlainLang_mem_NL}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.validPlainLang_mem_NL}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.NPreS, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA, Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA_ans, Complexity.LogProg.guessValidA_halts, Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le, Complexity.LogProg.narm_decides, Complexity.LogProg.validPlainLang, Complexity.NL, Complexity.logSpace}
\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ be the language of Boolean words $x$ for which there exist $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and
a canonical Boolean word $w$ such that $x=\mathrm{pairEncode}((1^n),w)$, where $(1^n)$
denotes the length-$n$ word of ones. Here $\mathrm{pairEncode}$ doubles each bit of its
first component, then appends $01$ and its second component. Then $L$ belongs to
nondeterministic logarithmic space: there is a
finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite number of work tapes
and a constant $c\in\mathbb N$ that halts on every input along every choice sequence of
a common length for that input, uses at most $c(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1)$ work-tape
cells on each such sequence, and accepts exactly the words in $L$.
\end{theorem}
